recall_prompt: Say how you would resolve x²/((x − 1)(x − 2)) into partial fractions — name each move in order, starting with what must be done before the form is written.
insider_note: Degree 2 over degree 2 is improper, so the answer starts with the constant 1, read straight from the leading coefficients; without that 1 in the form, no A and B can make the identity hold.

steps.label: Divide, then set up the form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Degree 2 over degree 2: improper, and both leading coefficients are 1, so the quotient is the constant 1. Then A over (x − 1) and B over (x − 2).
steps.memory_tip: Degree 2 over degree 2 is IMPROPER. Both leading coefficients are 1, so the quotient is just 1.

recall.must_convey: That equal degrees make the quotient the constant 1, and the form is 1 + A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 2).
accept: the degrees are equal so the quotient is one, then write one plus A over x minus one plus B over x minus two
improper with equal degrees so a constant one comes first and then one constant over each factor
one plus A by x minus 1 plus B by x minus 2
degrees same kabatti quotient one, tarvata A by x minus one plus B by x minus two rasali
write the constant one and then two fractions for the two linear factors

steps.why: x² over x² − 3x + 2 is 1 plus a proper fraction, because the degrees match and the leading coefficients are both 1. Without the 1 the identity x² = A(x − 2) + B(x − 1) has no solution, since the right side has no x² term.
common_mistakes: Writing A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 2) with no 1 in front.
Doing a full long division when the quotient can be read off the leading coefficients.

steps.label: Clear the denominators
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply by (x − 1)(x − 2). The 1 keeps the whole product; A keeps (x − 2), B keeps (x − 1).
steps.memory_tip: The 1 keeps the whole product (x − 1)(x − 2); A keeps (x − 2) and B keeps (x − 1).

recall.must_convey: That multiplying through gives x² = (x − 1)(x − 2) + A(x − 2) + B(x − 1).
accept: multiply both sides by x minus one into x minus two to get x squared equals x minus one into x minus two plus A into x minus two plus B into x minus one
clear the denominators and the one keeps the whole product
x squared equals the product plus A into x minus two plus B into x minus one
denominator tho multiply cheste x square equals x minus one x minus two plus A into x minus two plus B into x minus one
remove the fractions and keep the one term as the full product

steps.why: The quotient 1 multiplied by the denominator gives the product term, which supplies the x² that the A and B terms cannot. That is why the identity now balances.
common_mistakes: Writing x on the left instead of x².

steps.label: Find the constants
steps.margin_note: Third mark. x = 1 makes the product and the B term zero: 1 = −A. x = 2 makes the product and the A term zero: 4 = B.
steps.memory_tip: At each root the product vanishes too: x = 1 gives 1 = −A, and x = 2 gives 4 = B.

recall.must_convey: That x = 1 gives A = −1 and x = 2 gives B = 4.
accept: put x equals one to get A equals minus one and x equals two to get B equals four
the roots one and two give A minus one and B four
A minus one, B four
x equals one pedithe A minus one, x equals two pedithe B four
two substitutions at the roots give the two constants

steps.why: At a root of the denominator the product term vanishes as well as one constant term, so each substitution still isolates a single constant even with the quotient present.
common_mistakes: Putting x = 1 and writing A(1 − 2) = A instead of −A, giving A = 1.
Keeping the product (x − 1)(x − 2) on the right at x = 1; it is zero there.
Putting x = 2 and writing 2 instead of 2² = 4 on the left.

steps.label: Write the result
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The 1 comes first, then −1/(x − 1) + 4/(x − 2). This matches the answer the book prints for its practice question. Write the original fraction on the left.

recall.must_convey: That the fraction equals 1 − 1/(x − 1) + 4/(x − 2), with the constant 1 in front.
accept: the answer is one minus one over x minus one plus four over x minus two

steps.why: The constant quotient is part of the answer. All three terms with their signs make the resolved form the examiner marks.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the 1 in the final line.
Not checking: put x = 0 in the identity, 0 = 2 + 2 − 4. If the two sides differ, a constant is wrong.
